chunks: He lit a flame for the seeker, and illuminated a sign for the one who was impeded.
So he is Your trustworthy trustee, Your witness on the Day of Judgement, Your deputy as a blessing, and Your messenger of truth as mercy.
O Allah, distribute to him a share from Your Justice, and award him multiples of good by Your bounty.

O Allah, heighten his construction over the constructions of others, honour him when he comes to Thee, dignify his position before Thee, give him the intercession, and award him glory and distinction.
And bring us out (on Day of Judgement) among his party, neither ashamed, nor repentant, nor deviators, nor pledge-breakers, nor strayers, nor misleads.
ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes and supplications for the Holy Prophet in this text from Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Imam Ali’s sermon in *Nahj al-Balagha* employs rich metaphorical language, describing the Prophet as a 'torch for the seeker' and 'light for the holder,' emphasizing his role as the divine trust (*Amin*) and the ultimate mercy (*Rahma*) sent to guide humanity. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s spiritual authority and intercessory status, culminating in a petition for the supplicants to be gathered in his company on the Day of Resurrection free from shame or regret.
